title: The Sabbath: God's Gift of Rest
subtitle: A topical Bible study in four parts
author: doc-studio test

summary.topic: What the Bible teaches about the seventh-day Sabbath, from Creation to Jesus' ministry, and what it means for us today.
key_points: God blessed and sanctified the seventh day at Creation, before sin and before Israel existed (Genesis 2:1-3).
The fourth commandment asks us to *remember* the day and grounds it in Creation (Exodus 20:8-11).
Jesus called Himself "Lord also of the sabbath" and said it "was made for man" (Mark 2:27-28).
The Sabbath is meant to be a delight and a picture of the rest Jesus offers (Isaiah 58:13-14; Matthew 11:28).
summary.takeaway: The Sabbath is not a burden but a weekly gift: time set apart by the Creator to rest in Him.

blocks.title: Memory verse
blocks.text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. (Exodus 20:8, KJV)
1. Rest built into Creation
The first thing the Bible calls holy is not a place or a person but a day. At the end of Creation week God rested, blessed the seventh day and set it apart (Scripture: Genesis 2:2-3).

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.

God did not rest because He was tired. His rest marked a finished, "very good" work and invited humanity to share in it. Because this happened before sin and before the nation of Israel, the Sabbath belongs to all people (Inference from Genesis 2:1-3 and Mark 2:27).
He gave it to Adam as a day of rest. It was a memorial of the work of creation, and thus a sign of God's power and His love.
2. Remember: the fourth commandment
At Sinai God did not introduce a new day. He said **"Remember"**, pointing back to Creation, and named the day exactly: "the seventh day" (Scripture: Exodus 20:8-11).

Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work... For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the Lord blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.

rows: The blessing is on the day itself
blocks.caption: Table 1. The commandment repeats the Creation account (wording from the KJV).

blocks.text: 3. Jesus, Lord of the Sabbath
In Jesus' day the Sabbath had been loaded with human rules. Jesus did not set the day aside; He cleared away the burdens and showed what it was for (Scripture: Mark 2:27-28).
And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
The institutions that God has established are for the benefit of mankind.
If the Sabbath was made *for* us, keeping it is not about earning God's favour. It is about receiving time with Him that He has already given (Inference from Mark 2:27 and Matthew 11:28).
4. A delight, and a sign of deeper rest
If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable... Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord

Isaiah describes the Sabbath as "a delight". Jesus offers rest to all who "labour and are heavy laden" (Scripture: Matthew 11:28), and Hebrews speaks of a rest that "remaineth" for God's people (Scripture: Hebrews 4:9-10). The weekly Sabbath is a regular reminder of that rest in Him (Inference).
There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.
What it means for me

items: Plan ahead on Friday so the Sabbath hours are free for God, family and rest.
Choose activities that make the day a *delight*: worship, nature, visiting the sick, time with family.
Treat the Sabbath as an appointment with your Creator, not a list of don'ts.

blocks.text: Discussion questions

items: Genesis 2:3 says God blessed and sanctified the seventh day. Why do you think the first holy thing in the Bible is *time*?
Exodus 20:8 begins with "Remember". What does that word suggest about when the Sabbath began?
Jesus said "The sabbath was made for man" (Mark 2:27). How can this change the way we keep it?
Isaiah 58:13 calls the Sabbath "a delight". What would make your Sabbath a delight this week?
